root_cause: V9 KEEPER-RELEASE vetoes on worst cases, silently in two of them. s7453 (P2, Determined Acquisition): _keeper_release_primary_counts returns true because per_objective (3 VP, exclude_home false) counts home. That is a hard veto even though the AI loses home's VP for at most one scoring. Also no unit is within one move of home (Guard A/C 15-16" away, M8), so backups is empty. Both are silent returns, so no [KEEPER_RELEASE] line. s7454 (P1, Immovable Object, home excluded): the backup exists (Prosecutors 11"). The block is the max-roll threat radius M+12+6 = 26" + 3.79" range. P2's Custodian Guard Beta is ~29.5" away ('can reach it in one turn'), but it could only walk M+Advance 14" or charge a unit of ours near home. With the on-board check fixed, V9's other worst case also blocks: any enemy reserve 'can arrive' in round 2. Where B gained (A/B records, 2 seeds, horizon end of R2): s7454 B cut P2's secondaries (Forward Position / Centre Ground 15->8 and 10->5) by contesting the centre. s7453 B gained in material/Beacon. Both gains come from a durable unit forward, not from primary on home.
fix_summary: FIX_KEEPER_REACH (round 1 only, KEEPER_REACH_MAX_ROUND=1) widens _keeper_release_check where V9 would keep the keeper. (a) Primary that pays for home: priced instead of vetoed. Home VP for one scoring = per_objective/hold_min rules that count home + secondary 'home' hints. The best target must beat holding by KEEPER_RELEASE_MIN_GAIN + that VP. require_hold_home, hold_more and mechanic rules cannot be priced, so the keeper is kept. (b) Backup: if no unit can step onto home in one move, one of our units in reserves counts (it arrives from round 2). (c) Threat: the max-roll radius is re-checked with a realistic model. An enemy model within M+12" of home's range (move+Advance) is a threat. So is one within charge reach (M+12+1, +6 if it may advance and charge) of one of our models within range+6" of home (charge, then consolidate onto home). Reserves keep V9's rule, except in battle round 2 a unit explicitly in Strategic Reserves without Deep Strike cannot reach our zone. (d) A keeper released only this way makes a Normal move (keeps shooting/charging) to the objective it reaches soonest by Normal move, among those that beat holding (a lost race allowed; its penalty is in the score). Ties go by score, then distance. A secondary card that pays for home is added to the cost. V9 releases (reach empty) are unchanged. FIX_KEEPER_REACH=0 restores base. New log tag [KEEPER_REACH].

fires: Releases ([KEEPER_REACH] ... released) in replays to end of round 2, both players counted: s7453 1 (P2 Guard Beta, round 1). s7454, s7437, s7451, s7420, s7455, s7458, s7433: 0. It can only fire in battle round 1, at most once per player per game.
risks: Rounds 1-2: the released keeper leaves home empty for at least the enemy's next turn and our next command scoring. When the primary counts home (e.g. Determined Acquisition) that one scoring is lost; it is priced into the margin, but only if the reserve backup actually re-takes home. The reserve-arrival AI places reserves near objectives in general, not on our empty home specifically. If no unit returns, home can stay empty in rounds 3-5 and lose that rule's VP every scoring (3 VP x up to 4 = 12 VP on Determined Acquisition). This is the main full-game risk and the one place the one-round value check cannot see; a full-game bench in the Custodes mirror should check it. Cards that pay for home later (e.g. Defend Stronghold drawn from round 2: 3 VP a turn at the end of the opponent's turn) are not known in round 1; the keeper will be ~20" forward by then, so other units or reserves have to serve them. On the upside the effect lasts: a durable unit in the centre from round 2 helps Centre Ground, Forward Position, Engage on All Fronts and Beacon and denies the enemy the same cards (the s7454 A/B gain came from exactly that). This is the opposite of round 2's FAR_TRIP/OVERCOMMIT failure (units held back). Choosing the soonest objective can send the keeper into a 'lost race' at the centre (allowed on purpose; its penalty is in the score), which risks the unit against the whole enemy army in rounds 2-3. Base-code full-game A/B, 3 seeds each: s7453 alternative +15 VP mean; s7454 alternative -11 VP mean; both noisy, so the full-game effect is unproven. The release narration reuses V9's text ('our primary does not pay for it ... can re-take it in one move'), which is inaccurate for KEEPER-REACH releases; the [KEEPER_REACH] log line gives the real reason. The trigger is narrow (round 1 only, keeper not fragile, a target beats holding by >=5, our reserves non-empty), so it should fire rarely outside Custodes-style armies with deep-strike reserves.
